title: Pathway cost & latency decomposition harmonizer — per-route/model/customer attribution
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Build a backend service that synthesizes runtime telemetry, billing events, and routing metadata into a single, explainable per-route / per-model / per-customer cost and latency breakdown. This service (Pathway Harmonizer) will be the canonical source for Console dashboards, cost alerts, and tenant chargeback exports.

Background: Current pipelines produce fragmented outputs: runtime traces (latency, GPU time, kernel stats), quota/billing events (token counts, charge units), and routing metadata (route_id, model_variant, region). Downstream systems reconcile these data sources with ad-hoc heuristics, causing mismatches between Console dashboards and invoices. We need a deterministic, auditable decomposition that: attributes compute time and token-based cost to the originating route/model/customer, handles batching and shared-KV scenarios, and surfaces confidence/signature metadata for each attribution row.

Goals:
- Produce a daily and realtime (1m) feed of per-route/model/customer breakdown rows.
- Make attributions explainable with provenance (span ids, sample traces, aggregation window details).
- Correct for batching, multi-tenant GPUs, and KV cache hits/misses.
- Keep compute footprint low: incremental rollups and vectorized windowing.
- Provide backwards-compatible schema for existing Console dashboards and CSV chargeback exports.
acceptance_criteria: Realtime stream emits breakdown rows with route_id, model_id, customer_id, tokens, compute_ms, gpu_seconds, cost_estimate_usd, latency_p50/p95, attribution_confidence (0.0-1.0) within 1 minute of request completion.
Daily rollup job produces reconciled totals matching billing ledger within 0.5% for top 50 customers by spend after tunable correction factors.
Fallback heuristics documented and tested: when span-level linkage missing, attribute using probabilistic routing fingerprints and mark confidence <= 0.6.
Console visualizations (cost breakdown and latency waterfall) wired to new feed and show annotation links to trace samples for investigation.
End-to-end load test demonstrates sustained 5k reqs/s ingestion with <30s processing lag for realtime aggregation tier on current staging cluster size.
design_summary:
Two-tier architecture: (1) Ingest adapters normalize telemetry and billing events into a compact canonical event envelope (event_type, event_ts, route_id?, model_id?, request_id, span_id?, tokens, gpu_ms, raw_cost_units, reason_tags). (2) Harmonizer engine ingests the envelope stream, applies deterministic attribution rules, produces per-request micro-attributions, and writes both a realtime delta stream (Kafka topic) and incremental/day-level rollups to the analytical store. Attribution rules include: exact span-join (preferred), request-id join, batching-split algorithm (token-proportional and latency-proportional modes), and probabilistic fingerprint for orphaned records. Confidence score is computed from join type, presence of KV cache hit flag, and batching ambiguity.

Key trade-offs: store micro-attributions for 30 days for debugging vs only keeping rollups. We keep micro-attributions for 30 days in compressed Parquet and expose sampled traces in stable S3 paths for audits.

Dataflows & retention: raw envelopes kept 14 days in topic; micro-attributions kept 30 days; daily rollups retained for 3 years.
data_schema: Output row schema (flat): [route_id:string, model_id:string, customer_id:string, request_id:string, span_id:string, timestamp:ISO8601, tokens:int, input_tokens:int, output_tokens:int, compute_ms:float, gpu_seconds:float, raw_cost_units:float, cost_usd:float, latency_ms:float, p50_latency_ms:float, p95_latency_ms:float, kv_cache_hit:boolean, batch_size:int, attribution_method:string, attribution_confidence:float, provenance_links:list_of_urls]
aggregation_strategy: Realtime tier: 1m tumbling windows per (route_id, model_id, customer_id) that ingest micro-attributions and emit delta rows to Console topics. Daily tier: map-reduce style job that reconciles realtime deltas with billing ledger, applies correction factors (batch-splitting residuals, cross-tenant GPU noise), and emits final daily rollups. Correction factors are computed per-model-class and per-hardware-class using sampling and historical reconcilers.
pipeline_steps: Adapter: normalize incoming telemetry & billing events -> canonical envelope
Joiner: span/request-level join to build micro-attribution candidates
Splitter: batching split algorithm to assign GPU time and tokens across requests in a batch
Harmonizer: deterministic rule engine produces final attribution row with confidence
Emitter: realtime Kafka topic + short-term Parquet store for micro-attributions
Rollup job: reconcile with billing ledger, apply corrections, write final daily rollups to warehouse
Exporter: CSV/Parquet chargeback export + Console API surface
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (canary): wire realtime topic to Console internal 'cost-debug' dashboards for 10 internal customers, compare with current Console and ledger. Phase 2: enable daily rollups for all internal customers and preview for top 10 customers opt-in. Phase 3: GA and replace legacy feed; run two-week shadow checks for parity and then flip. Rollback path: disable harmonizer consumer and fall back to legacy aggregator topics.

Safety: run reconciler in a separate namespace with read-only access to billing ledger until validated; add throttles to avoid overloading warehouse queries.
metrics: emitted_rows/s, processing_lag_seconds (95th), reconcile_delta_percentile (top-50-customers), attribution_confidence_distribution, KV_cache_hit_rate_by_route, micro-attribution_storage_bytes
performance_targets: Realtime processing lag p95 < 60s at 5k eps; daily rollup job complete < 2h for 24h window for current dataset; reconciliation delta <0.5% for top 50 customers after correction; CPU cost for harmonizer service < $0.02 per 1k requests (estimated).
monitoring_queries: select sum(cost_usd) from daily_rollups where date = today() group by customer_id order by sum desc limit 50
comments: 2026-02-11 | Asha Patel: Initial draft PRD posted. Outline includes canonical envelope and confidence model. Asked infra for Kafka retention increase for telemetry topics.
2026-02-18 | Ravi Menon (PM): Reviewed trade-offs. PM asks to ensure cumulative billing parity checks are part of acceptance criteria — added reconciliation threshold metric.
2026-02-26 | Priya Singh (Infra): Confirmed Kafka cluster can support increased retention for 14 days in staging; recommended compression changes to reduce storage cost.
2026-03-03 | Design review by Mei Chen: requested UI annotation affordances to link breakdown rows to trace samples and flagged the need for privacy review for sampled traces — added to design notes.
2026-03-09 | Liam O'Connor: Implemented adapter for runtime telemetry and pushed schema v0.1. Added unit tests for batching split algorithm (token-proportional mode).
2026-03-12 | QA: smoke tests passed on canary with internal customers; reconciliation delta at 0.34% for canary group. Next: expand canary to additional teams and run 7-day parity run.
last_qa_notes: Smoke pass metrics: p95 processing lag = 42s, attribution_confidence median = 0.84, reconciliation delta (canary) = 0.34%. Found edge case when batch_size=1 and KV cache flag missing: attribution_method falls back to probabilistic_fingerprint and confidence=0.58; created follow-up ENG-365850 to add a KV-propagation shim in the runtime headers.
implementation_notes: Prefer Rust-based Harmonizer engine for deterministic performance and stable memory use. Use ksqlDB or Flink for realtime tumbling windows and a daily Spark job for heavy reconciliation. Provide a lightweight Python library for Console to fetch and annotate rows. Use Parquet + partitioned S3 for micro-attribution storage and BigQuery/Warehouse for daily rollups. Ensure schema evolution path with clear versioning and migration scripts.
